The same National Portrait Gallery biography records 27 consecutive Ted Heath broadcasts on the radio program Top Ten.

ted-heath.limitations: The gallery's overview describes the band's multi-year activity, not specific personnel or recording credits for each film.
ted-heath.summary: British trombonist and bandleader Ted Heath led a swing orchestra associated with London Palladium performances and films from 1946 through 1960.
ted-heath.why_it_matters: The National Portrait Gallery preserves Heath's professional band history and performance venues.

evidence.claim: Fresh Sound's reissue notes identify Ruby Braff, Jimmy Jones, Milt Hinton and Jo Jones on the 1954 Miss Teddi King sessions.
The label separately credits Bob Brookmeyer, Billy Taylor, Milt Hinton and Osie Johnson on 1955 Now in Vogue sessions.

teddi-king.limitations: Credits are specific to the two source LPs; no claim that every musician plays every track.
teddi-king.summary: American jazz singer Teddi King recorded intimate Storyville sessions in 1954 and 1955 with swing musicians including Ruby Braff and Bob Brookmeyer.
teddi-king.why_it_matters: Documents a distinct instrumental or vocal contribution and its musical context.

evidence.claim: Concord's label biography says Charles was part of the Jazz Composers Workshop from 1953 to 1955.
Concord identifies his 1955 Evolution quartet album with J.R. Monterose and Charles Mingus.

teddy-charles.limitations: Only claims recorded in the cited artist, label, institution or original archive are included; crossovers are not classified exclusively as jazz.
teddy-charles.summary: American vibraphonist Teddy Charles explored bebop and Third Stream jazz, leading Prestige sessions and working with Charles Mingus.
teddy-charles.why_it_matters: Documents specific recordings, ensembles or performance roles and their place in jazz or adjacent genres.

evidence.claim: Concord's Teddy Edwards artist biography says he switched to tenor saxophone while working with Howard McGhee after moving to Los Angeles.
Concord lists Edwards' Contemporary Records albums Teddy's Ready and a reunion with McGhee titled Together Again! among his 1960-62 recordings.
Concord identifies Sunset Eyes as an original composition of tenor saxophonist Teddy Edwards.

teddy-edwards.limitations: The record-label biography documents general group work and album titles but not personnel or recording dates for every track.
teddy-edwards.summary: Los Angeles tenor saxophonist Teddy Edwards worked with Howard McGhee and recorded the Contemporary albums Teddy's Ready and Together Again! in the 1960s.
teddy-edwards.why_it_matters: The label responsible for original Contemporary releases gives identifiable session series and musician associations.

evidence.claim: Hill led a successful big band during the 1930s.
Hill later managed Minton's Playhouse, home to formative bebop jam sessions.

teddy-hill.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
teddy-hill.summary: Bandleader Teddy Hill led a successful 1930s swing orchestra and later managed Harlem's Minton's Playhouse, where after-hours jam sessions fostered early bebop.
teddy-hill.why_it_matters: His nightclub leadership supported the experimental culture of bebop.

evidence.claim: Concord original Bearcat notes list Teddy Smith with Clifford Jordan, Cedar Walton and J.C. Moses.
Fresh Sound's archival reissue credits bassist Teddy Smith on Kenny Dorham Matador with Jackie McLean, Bobby Timmons and J.C. Moses, recorded in New York on April 15, 1962.
Fresh Sound explicitly separates the 1961 Jazz Workshop album Inta Somethin', which features Leroy Vinnegar on bass, from Teddy Smith's April 1962 Matador album.

teddy-smith.limitations: Fresh Sound's compilation includes a different bassist on the live Inta Somethin' session: Smith is credited only on Matador.
teddy-smith.summary: Bassist Teddy Smith played with Clifford Jordan and Cedar Walton on Bearcat and with Kenny Dorham and Jackie McLean on the 1962 Matador session.
teddy-smith.why_it_matters: Two label catalog records document distinct sessions and named ensembles for an otherwise sparsely biographed bassist.

evidence.claim: Swiss national historical dictionary describes Teddy Stauffer founding Teddy and His Band in Bern in 1928 and a 1936 Delphi engagement in Berlin.
Swissinfo's archive of a Swiss Radio International jazz program identifies Teddy Stauffer and His Original Teddies recording Moeni Stomp in 1940, source Elite SJLP 6306.
Deutsche Biographie documents 100-plus Telefunken recordings by Stauffer's orchestra in 1936-1939 and EliteDecca recordings in 1940-1941.

teddy-stauffer.limitations: The 1940 recording is dated by the Swiss broadcaster's retrospective playlist; the 2008 broadcast page is not an original issue date.
teddy-stauffer.summary: Swiss saxophonist Teddy Stauffer led the Original Teddies swing orchestra in Berlin and recorded Moeni Stomp for Elite in 1940.
teddy-stauffer.why_it_matters: Swiss historical and broadcast archives preserve ensemble identity, a specific 1940 recording and contemporary swing context.

evidence.claim: Miles Davis's official estate site credits Teo Macero as a Columbia staff producer who began working with Davis in 1959.
The Miles Davis estate describes Macero's cutting, looping, mixing and editing of Davis sessions as crucial to the final Columbia albums.
Concord identifies Teo Macero as composer and tenor saxophonist on the Third Stream project Teo, with Mal Waldron and Teddy Charles in the Prestige Jazz Quartet.

teo-macero.limitations: The official Miles Davis site describes his broader production period, while the Prestige quartet credits refer to a specific Macero-led album, not a Miles Davis band.
teo-macero.summary: Producer and tenor saxophonist Teo Macero shaped Miles Davis's Columbia albums through studio editing and recorded the Third Stream album Teo.
teo-macero.why_it_matters: Miles Davis's estate confirms the creative role of Macero's studio edits and Concord identifies his own instrumental work outside record production.

evidence.claim: Blue Note identifies Flow (2005) as a Blanchard leader album produced by Herbie Hancock.
The label identifies Magnetic (2013) as a new-quintet project with guest appearances by Ron Carter, Lionel Loueke and Ravi Coltrane.

terence-blanchard.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
terence-blanchard.summary: Trumpeter Terence Blanchard recorded the Herbie Hancock-produced Flow in 2005 and led Magnetic in 2013, featuring Ron Carter and Lionel Loueke.
terence-blanchard.why_it_matters: His work connects post-bop trumpet improvisation with film and large-ensemble composition.

evidence.claim: Concord's reissue notes say Terry Callier recorded his debut The New Folk Sound of Terry Callier in 1965, with Terbour Attenborough and John Tweedle.
Pitchfork's archival retrospective identifies Callier's 1972 Occasional Rain, What Color Is Love and 1973 I Just Can't Help Myself as productions by Charles Stepney on Cadet.

identity_resolution.note: Concord identifies the Chicago guitarist/singer on the 1965-recorded Prestige release; the independent 1972 Cadet album historical review identifies the same Chicago songwriter by original album, genre and named producer, not by a bare MusicBrainz P434 association.

terry-callier.limitations: Originally insufficient_evidence; dates distinguish the 1965 Prestige debut recording from its later issue and do not assume that its 1965 session date is the first retail release.
terry-callier.summary: Chicago vocalist-guitarist Terry Callier recorded The New Folk Sound in 1965 and made the Cadet albums Occasional Rain and What Color Is Love in 1972.
terry-callier.why_it_matters: Concord's archival recording notes and a contemporary Chess catalog establish specific albums across his early folk and later soul-jazz periods.

evidence.claim: Terumasa Hino recorded 'Taro's Mood' in 1973 with pianist Mikio Masuda and drummer Motohiko Hino.
Its quartet personnel include Hino, Masuda, Ikeda and Motohiko Hino.

terumasa-hino.limitations: Research is source-specific; credits denote actual documented roles, not an exhaustive discography.
terumasa-hino.summary: Trumpeter Terumasa Hino recorded 'Taro's Mood' in June 1973 with pianist Mikio Masuda, bassist Yoshio Ikeda and drummer Motohiko Hino.
terumasa-hino.why_it_matters: Small-group Japanese jazz trumpet and rhythm section interplay.

evidence.claim: The Teddy Wilson 1939 original-matrix catalog credits Thelma Carpenter on vocals for Love Grows On The White Oak Tree (matrix B24931-A), recorded July 26, 1939 and issued on Brunswick 8455.
The same Brunswick 8455 matrix catalog lists her on This Is The Moment (B24932-A) at the July 26, 1939 session, excluding her from the instrumental Early Session Hop side.

Jasmine Records' original release notes for The Eddie Cantor Sessions (JASMCD2786) identify Thelma Carpenter as the singer in surviving 1945-46 Eddie Cantor Show air-checks, issued together in June 2024.

thelma-carpenter.limitations: The 1939 Brunswick sides are documented by a specialist original-matrix reconstruction, not a directly examined 78 shellac label. Jasmine's 2024 CD reissues radio material broadcast in 1945-46; 2024 is not the performance year.
thelma-carpenter.summary: Jazz vocalist Thelma Carpenter sang on Teddy Wilson's 1939 Brunswick sides and made 1945-46 radio broadcasts for Eddie Cantor.
thelma-carpenter.why_it_matters: A reconstructed Brunswick original-matrix catalog and Jasmine's first-party restoration of air-checks verify two distinct musical periods.

evidence.claim: His official biography names saxophone, flute and duduk as instruments.
His official performance history lists Soft Machine since 2016 and collaborations with Robert Fripp.

theo-travis.summary: British saxophonist and flautist Theo Travis leads Double Talk and has performed with Soft Machine and Robert Fripp.
theo-travis.why_it_matters: Documents this musician's distinctive role in jazz and related music.

evidence.claim: Spassov's official biography describes his compositions as blending folk music with jazz and classical music.
It lists performances with Dave Liebman, Andy Sheppard and Rabih Abou-Khalil.

theodosii-spassov.limitations: Artist-level historical synopsis; specific session credits restricted to cited primary material.
theodosii-spassov.summary: Bulgarian kaval virtuoso Theodosii Spassov integrates folk flute, jazz and classical music in original compositions and collaborations.
theodosii-spassov.why_it_matters: Documents concrete genre, performance and recording contributions to a diverse jazz catalog.

evidence.claim: Smithsonian National Museum of American History identifies Thomas A. Dorsey's blues persona Georgia Tom and his direction of the Pilgrim Baptist Church choir in Chicago.
Library of Congress Recording Registry identifies its 1973 Precious Lord recording as featuring Thomas A. Dorsey narrating his life and performances of his gospel works.
Library of Congress National Recording Preservation Board historical essay links Dorsey's Georgia Tom blues work with Tampa Red and his later gospel composition.

thomas-a-dorsey.limitations: The Smithsonian museum's sixty-year figure describes choir leadership, not a continuously documented set of dates; 1973 belongs to the Precious Lord recording, not the Library of Congress induction year (2002).
thomas-a-dorsey.summary: Pianist Thomas A. Dorsey recorded blues as Georgia Tom, directed Pilgrim Baptist Church's choir and narrated his life on 1973's Precious Lord.
thomas-a-dorsey.why_it_matters: Smithsonian and Library of Congress sources document his blues-to-gospel transition and the 1973 Precious Lord recording preserved in the National Recording Registry.

evidence.claim: Original NABEL 4642 LP credits for ChoralConcert name Thomas Klemm on saxophone and flute, Karl Scharnweber on organ and Wolfgang Schmiedt on guitar; recording took place July 26-28, 1990.
Original BuschFunk publisher roster lists Thomas Klemm with Pascal von Wroblewsky and Axel Donner on their 1991 collaboration and on So Easy issued in 1993.
The Thuringian archive's 1996 ChoralConcert poster directly credits Thomas Klemm on saxophone and flutes with Scharnweber and Schmiedt in a July 17 program.

thomas-klemm.limitations: The 2013 NABEL digital issue is not the July 1990 session; the 1996 ChoralConcert evidence is a performance poster, not an album session. Independent identity supported by named ensembles, not an inferred generic jazz career.
thomas-klemm.summary: German saxophonist Thomas Klemm recorded ChoralConcert with Karl Scharnweber and Wolfgang Schmiedt in 1990 and joined Wroblewsky and Donner in 1991.
thomas-klemm.why_it_matters: Original NABEL LP credits, a music publisher's recording list and an institutional concert-poster archive identify specific instruments and ensembles.

evidence.claim: Vic Firth's original artist profile credits Thomas Lang with the Vienna Art Orchestra and his 1995 solo release Mediator.
Vic Firth's original studio interview profile says Lang began drums aged five and studied at the Vienna Conservatory.
Meinl Cymbals' artist interview documents Lang's classical musical training and Los Angeles studio practice.

thomas-lang.limitations: His career includes pop and rock, so those collaborators are not mislabeled as jazz projects.
thomas-lang.summary: Austrian drummer Thomas Lang studied at the Vienna Conservatory, worked with the Vienna Art Orchestra and released the solo album Mediator.
thomas-lang.why_it_matters: Original Vic Firth artist credits and a separate Meinl studio interview identify the working drummer.

evidence.claim: The album Nice 'n' Easy appeared on OKeh/Sony in 2018.
The album was his first recording with the NDR Big Band.
Its featured partners include pianist Frank Chastenier, bassist Dieter Ilg and drummer Wolfgang Haffner.

thomas-quasthoff.limitations: Classical vocalist with a documented jazz project; no claim of jazz-only specialization.
thomas-quasthoff.summary: Classical baritone Thomas Quasthoff recorded jazz standards on Nice 'n' Easy with the NDR Big Band in 2018, joined by Frank Chastenier and Dieter Ilg.
thomas-quasthoff.why_it_matters: His jazz album adapts a major classical singer's technique to swing standards.

evidence.claim: ECM credits Thomas T Dahl on guitar in Rubicon beside Mats Eilertsen, Trygve Seim, Eirik Hegdal, Rob Waring, Harmen Fraanje and Olavi Louhivuori.
The Rubicon septet recording took place in May 2015 at Rainbow Studio, Oslo, with compositions developed for the Vossajazz Festival.

thomas-t-dahl.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
thomas-t-dahl.summary: Norwegian guitarist Thomas T Dahl joined Mats Eilertsen's septet for Rubicon, recorded at Rainbow Studio in Oslo in May 2015.
thomas-t-dahl.why_it_matters: His guitar joins piano, reeds and marimba in Eilertsen's spacious Norwegian ensemble writing.

evidence.claim: Mockroot released February 17 2015 on Nonesuch
Trio includes Sam Minaie and Arthur Hnatek

tigran-hamasyan.limitations: Source-specific musical details; does not establish exhaustive discography.
tigran-hamasyan.summary: Armenian jazz pianist Tigran Hamasyan's 'Mockroot' (2015) mixes Armenian folk songs, intricate jazz rhythms, rock, voice and electronic textures.
tigran-hamasyan.why_it_matters: Rhythmic cross-pollination of Armenian folk material and contemporary improvisation

evidence.claim: Edition Records credits Garland with tenor and soprano saxophones, bass clarinet and flute on Songs to the North Sky, alongside John Patitucci and Asaf Sirkis.
The album was released June 2, 2014, with sessions at Eastcote Studio London, Curtis Schwartz's studio and The Sage Gateshead for strings.

tim-garland.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
tim-garland.summary: British reed player Tim Garland released Songs to the North Sky in 2014, combining saxophones and bass clarinet with strings, piano and percussion.
tim-garland.why_it_matters: Garland's writing fuses improvising jazz soloists with orchestral string textures.

evidence.claim: His official biography names Nigel Clark and Roy Percy in the Tim Kliphuis Trio.
It identifies Reflecting the Seasons and Brandenburg among his Sony Classical projects.

tim-kliphuis.limitations: Artist biography covers several ensembles; credits are limited to explicitly named trio.
tim-kliphuis.summary: Dutch violinist Tim Kliphuis blends gypsy jazz, folk and classical music. His trio includes guitarist Nigel Clark and bassist Roy Percy, alongside orchestral projects.
tim-kliphuis.why_it_matters: Highlights string improvisation and gypsy jazz in classical settings.

evidence.claim: Arena's official discography dates Don't Ask to 1994 and lists Chains and Sorrento Moon.
Her official site dates Love Saves to 2023 and lists Church and Dancing on Thin Ice.

tina-arena.limitations: Only claims recorded in the cited artist, label, institution or original archive are included; crossovers are not classified exclusively as jazz.
tina-arena.summary: Australian singer Tina Arena records pop ballads in English and French, with releases including Don't Ask and the later Love Saves.
tina-arena.why_it_matters: Documents specific recordings, ensembles or performance roles and their place in jazz or adjacent genres.

evidence.claim: Minor Move was recorded in 1958 and first released in 1980.
Its musicians included Lee Morgan, Sonny Clark, Doug Watkins and Art Blakey.

tina-brooks.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
tina-brooks.summary: Tenor saxophonist Tina Brooks recorded Minor Move in 1958 with Lee Morgan, Sonny Clark, Doug Watkins and Art Blakey; the hard-bop album was unreleased until 1980.
tina-brooks.why_it_matters: His scarce releases preserve a singular hard-bop tenor sound.

evidence.claim: The Royal Welsh College biography says May studied classical singing with Eileen Price at University College Cardiff.
The institutional biography credits a 2003 award for services to jazz education from the International Association for Jazz Education.

tina-may.limitations: Archived institutional bio appears to use present tense although May died in 2022; summary excludes present-tense career claims.
tina-may.summary: British jazz singer Tina May studied classical singing at Cardiff and was awarded a jazz education honor in 2003.
tina-may.why_it_matters: Documents this musician's distinctive role in jazz and related music.

evidence.claim: Trumpeter Tom Browne's official artist biography identifies him as an early signee to GRP Records after an introduction to producers Dave Grusin and Larry Rosen.
The artist's official bio names Funkin' For Jamaica and Thighs High among his GRP jazz-funk recordings.
Innervision Records' 2020 announcement confirms it signed jazz trumpeter Tom Browne and describes his decades of crossover releases.

tom-browne.limitations: The artist's general biography mentions numerous projects but not their exact session lineups or original release dates.
tom-browne.summary: Trumpeter Tom Browne joined the emerging GRP Records roster and mixed jazz improvisation with funk on hits such as Funkin' for Jamaica and Thighs High.
tom-browne.why_it_matters: A first-person artist biography and label release connect Browne's instrument, recorded crossover projects and GRP.

evidence.claim: Gaebel founded his own big band in Cologne in 2005.
His debut album Introducing: Myself appeared in 2005.
He studied trombone, drums and jazz vocals in Amsterdam.

tom-gaebel.limitations: Artist biography supports career trajectory; descriptions are stylistic rather than historic session details.
tom-gaebel.summary: German singer Tom Gaebel began leading his own big band in Cologne in 2005. His debut Introducing: Myself mixes swing singing and easy-listening arrangements.
tom-gaebel.why_it_matters: His self-produced concert repertoire continues the German big-band vocal tradition.

evidence.claim: Craft Latino's Metiendo mano! history credits Tom Malone on tuba within the brass section of Willie Colon and Ruben Blades's 1977 album.
Concord lists Tom Malone in the horn personnel for Ron Carter's Parade along with Urbie Green, Jon Faddis and Jerry Dodgion.
Concord also lists Tom Malone among the session musicians on Paulinho Da Costa's Happy People.

tom-malone.limitations: The confirmed tuba credit belongs to the 1977 salsa album; the Parade listing does not independently specify Malone's instrument.
tom-malone.summary: Multi-brass session musician Tom Malone played tuba on Willie Colon and Ruben Blades's Metiendo mano! and joined Ron Carter's horn section on Parade.
tom-malone.why_it_matters: Craft's reissue notes and Concord's Ron Carter album credits connect Malone to two historically documented, stylistically distinct sessions.

evidence.claim: Brownswood names Kareem Dayes on cello, Tom Herbert on bass, and Shabaka Hutchings and Nubya Garcia on woodwinds for Voices of Bishara.
Brownswood identifies November 2022 as the album release period and describes Skinner as an original member of Sons of Kemet.

tom-skinner.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
tom-skinner.summary: Drummer-composer Tom Skinner released Voices of Bishara in November 2022 with Nubya Garcia, Shabaka Hutchings, Tom Herbert and Kareem Dayes.
tom-skinner.why_it_matters: His London ensemble connects contemporary improvisation to the cello-led music of Abdul Wadud.

evidence.claim: Fresh Sound documents Thomas Talbert arranging, conducting and producing Patty McGovern's Atlantic 1245 Wednesday's Child, recorded in New York in August 1956.
Original track credits identify Wednesday's Child (Talbert-McGovern), Winter Song (Talbert-Wolfe) and Summer Rain (Talbert-McGovern).
The separate Kai Winding archival reissue Bop City credits Tom Talbert as composer of The Moonshower on an April 27, 1951 recording.

tom-talbert.limitations: August 1956 McGovern Atlantic sessions differ from February 1957 Decca tracks in the same reissue. Talbert wrote The Moonshower; no instrumental performance is inferred.
tom-talbert.summary: Arranger Tom Talbert produced Patty McGovern's 1956 Atlantic album Wednesday's Child and composed The Moonshower, recorded by Kai Winding in 1951.
tom-talbert.why_it_matters: Archival restorations of Atlantic and Winding original albums preserve specific composing, arranging and production credits.

evidence.claim: Sy Oliver became principal arranger around 1939
Sinatra joined Dorsey orchestra in 1940

tommy-dorsey.limitations: Specific sourced music facts, not a comprehensive discography.
tommy-dorsey.summary: Swing trombonist Tommy Dorsey's orchestra paired Sy Oliver's hot arrangements with the 1940 debut of vocalist Frank Sinatra; hear 'Opus One'.
tommy-dorsey.why_it_matters: Influential swing band combining smooth trombone sound and hot charts

evidence.claim: His official biography credits Chet Atkins as friend, mentor and collaborator.
The biography describes his album Living in the Light as combining jazz, classical, roots and acoustic pop.

tommy-emmanuel.limitations: Short artist-level account only; do not infer unlisted session or ensemble personnel.
tommy-emmanuel.summary: Australian guitarist Tommy Emmanuel developed a percussive fingerstyle approach and recorded with Chet Atkins while exploring jazz, pop and roots music.
tommy-emmanuel.why_it_matters: Adds a documented performer or composer and a specific musical contribution to the catalog.

evidence.claim: The Skatalites identify McCook as a tenor saxophonist and flutist who studied at Alpha School.
Their biography says he recorded Exodus in November 1963 with future Skatalites musicians.

tommy-mccook.limitations: Band-maintained artist history; avoid unsupported claims about genre invention.
tommy-mccook.summary: Jamaican tenor saxophonist and flutist Tommy McCook helped shape ska with the Skatalites after studying jazz. His recording career also included the Supersonics.
tommy-mccook.why_it_matters: Shows the jazz background underpinning Jamaican ska and rocksteady.

evidence.claim: Time T-70008 was recorded January 19, 1960 in New York with Tommy Turrentine on trumpet, Julian Priester on trombone, Stanley Turrentine on tenor, Horace Parlan on piano, Bob Boswell on bass and Max Roach on drums.
Fresh Sound lists Gunga Din, Times Up and Too Clean as compositions by Tommy Turrentine, Webb City by Bud Powell and Blues for J.P. by Horace Parlan, separating authorship from performance.

tommy-turrentine.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
tommy-turrentine.summary: Hard-bop trumpeter Tommy Turrentine led a Time Records session in New York on January 19, 1960 with Stanley Turrentine, Horace Parlan and Max Roach.
tommy-turrentine.why_it_matters: A documented 1960 sextet album resolves the earlier vague sideman-only narrative and distinguishes his trumpet from his brother Stanley's tenor.

evidence.claim: Concord states Bennett created his own Improv label in the mid-1970s.
The label lists Together Again with pianist Bill Evans and Rodgers and Hart albums with the Ruby Braff-George Barnes Quartet.

tony-bennett.limitations: Artist-level historical synopsis; specific session credits restricted to cited primary material.
tony-bennett.summary: American singer Tony Bennett performed jazz standards with small groups and made a series of independent Improv recordings in the 1970s.
tony-bennett.why_it_matters: Documents concrete genre, performance and recording contributions to a diverse jazz catalog.

evidence.claim: Original The Necks trio includes Buck, Abrahams and Swanton
Active as the original trio since 1986

tony-buck.limitations: Source-specific musical details, not a complete discography.
tony-buck.summary: Australian drummer Tony Buck co-founded improvised-music trio The Necks with Chris Abrahams and Lloyd Swanton in 1986; its hypnotic music unfolds slowly.
tony-buck.why_it_matters: Long-form collaborative improvisation and patient rhythmic development

evidence.claim: Austin Jazz Society identifies Campise primarily as a tenor saxophonist and flutist.
Its Hall of Fame profile records his Stan Kenton orchestra association and 1984 move to Austin.

tony-campise.limitations: Hall of Fame retrospective; no unverified individual recording titles.
tony-campise.summary: Houston-born saxophonist and flutist Tony Campise joined Stan Kenton's orchestra in the 1970s and later settled in Austin, where he worked in jazz education.
tony-campise.why_it_matters: Documents a Texas saxophone tradition within big-band and small-group playing.

evidence.claim: Official biography identifies Buddy Rich, Gary Burton and Steps Ahead among jazz credits
The Chapman Stick became integral to his electric work

tony-levin.limitations: Source-specific musical details; does not establish exhaustive discography.
tony-levin.summary: Bassist Tony Levin's jazz credits include Buddy Rich, Gary Burton and Steps Ahead; his Chapman Stick work also shaped progressive jazz-rock projects.
tony-levin.why_it_matters: Jazz-and-rock crossover bassist; important as supporting/ensemble musician

evidence.claim: Big Round Records biography places Oxley as house drummer at Ronnie Scott's after his move to London in 1966.
The label identifies his 1969 quintet and its album Baptized Traveller.

tony-oxley.summary: British drummer Tony Oxley worked as house drummer at Ronnie Scott's and recorded the exploratory album Baptized Traveller in 1969.
tony-oxley.why_it_matters: Documents this musician's distinctive role in jazz and related music.

evidence.claim: The Library of Congress lists Tony Sbarbaro on traps in the Original Dixieland Jazz Band's Dixieland Jass Band One-Step recorded February 26, 1917 in New York, Victor 18255.
The Library of Congress band biography names Sbarbaro as drummer alongside Nick LaRocca, Eddie Edwards, Larry Shields and Henry Ragas.
Smithsonian Folkways credits Tony Sbarbaro on drums for the Original Dixieland Jazz Band's Livery Stable Blues.

tony-sbarbaro.limitations: The Library of Congress calls the band's 1917 discs the earliest issued jazz records; that does not mean jazz began with this group.
tony-sbarbaro.summary: Drummer Tony Sbarbaro played in the Original Dixieland Jazz Band, appearing on the Victor recording Dixieland Jass Band One-Step made in New York in 1917.
tony-sbarbaro.why_it_matters: Library of Congress original Victor session metadata and Smithsonian performer credits directly establish his instrument and a historically important early jazz recording.

evidence.claim: His official biography says he attended New School University in New York in 2001.
It identifies Irish Heart as his 2006 ACT debut album.

torsten-goods.limitations: Official autobiography is promotional; competition rankings omitted.
torsten-goods.summary: German guitarist and singer Torsten Goods draws on jazz, blues, soul and pop. After studying in New York, he released Irish Heart on ACT in 2006.
torsten-goods.why_it_matters: Illustrates jazz guitar and vocal crossover in contemporary Europe.

evidence.claim: Norwegian scholarly music encyclopedia SNL records Totti Bergh performing with Kjell Karlsen orchestras from 1955 to 1962 and founding a quintet with Laila Dalseth in 1979.
Gemini Records' catalog metadata identifies Totti Bergh and Al Cohn as co-leading saxophonists on Tenor Gladness (GMCD53).
Gemini's label-supplied catalog lists Totti Bergh with Plas Johnson on On the Trail! (GMCD78), with the recorded compositions itemized.

totti-bergh.limitations: SNL is a specialist-authored institutional reference rather than a first-party label; Gemini catalog dates may reflect later reissues. No birth-date claim is made.
totti-bergh.summary: Norwegian tenor saxophonist Totti Bergh performed with Al Cohn on Tenor Gladness and with Plas Johnson on On the Trail!, both for Gemini.
totti-bergh.why_it_matters: An original Norwegian music scholar biography and Gemini album credits document separate ensemble work and recordings.

evidence.claim: His official biography identifies his debut album Ali on Broadway as released in 1994.
The same biography says he formed the nine-player Absolut Orchestra in 2001.

toufic-farroukh.limitations: Artist biography supports these broad credits; no track-by-track session personnel inferred.
toufic-farroukh.summary: Lebanese-born saxophonist Toufic Farroukh composes jazz with Middle Eastern timbres and recorded Ali on Broadway and Drab Zeen.
toufic-farroukh.why_it_matters: Documents a distinctive jazz crossover artist with artist-authored album or ensemble facts.

evidence.claim: Blue Note announced Trombone Shorty Parking Lot Symphony as a 12-track record released on April 28, 2017 and produced by Chris Seefried.
Blue Note says Parking Lot Symphony contains 10 new original compositions plus Allen Toussaint Here Come the Girls and the Meters It Aint No Use as covers.
The Blue Note No Good Time announcement explicitly calls Trombone Shorty Troy Andrews and credits his singing, trombone, trumpet, keys and drums on that named single.

trombone-shorty.limitations: Parking Lot Symphony is Blue Note debut, not Troy Andrews first album; announcement and later reviews cannot certify every instrumental part on all 12 tracks.
trombone-shorty.summary: Trombonist Troy Andrews led Trombone Shorty and Orleans Avenue, debuting on Blue Note in 2017 with Chris Seefried-produced Parking Lot Symphony.
trombone-shorty.why_it_matters: The original Blue Note album announcement documents stage identity, recording producer, original and cover tracks, and stylistic fusion.

evidence.claim: ECM lists Different Rivers and Helsinki Songs under Trygve Seim.
ECM identifies Our Time as a collaboration between Seim and Frode Haltli.

trygve-seim.limitations: ECM artist discography gives release identities but not every track personnel.
trygve-seim.summary: Norwegian saxophonist and composer Trygve Seim recorded Different Rivers and Helsinki Songs for ECM, as well as the duo album Our Time with Frode Haltli.
trygve-seim.why_it_matters: Maps the ECM strand of Nordic improvisation and chamber-oriented jazz.

evidence.claim: Washington played in Smiley Lewis's band on Imperial releases including Tee-Nah-Nah.
His solo album New Orleans Piano Professor was issued by Rounder in 1983.
His style blended ragtime, blues and boogie-woogie.

tuts-washington.limitations: Tulane historic-music project documents ensemble and album, not precise instrument personnel on every song.
tuts-washington.summary: New Orleans pianist Tuts Washington worked with guitarist Smiley Lewis on Imperial sides such as Tee-Nah-Nah. His solo piano album New Orleans Piano Professor came out in 1983.
tuts-washington.why_it_matters: His work connects ragtime, boogie-woogie and rhythm-and-blues piano in New Orleans.

evidence.claim: Craft Recordings says Tyrone Brown replaced founding Catalyst bassist Alphonso Johnson after the Philadelphia group's self-titled debut.
Concord's Pat Martino East! credits list Tyrone Brown with Eddie Green, Ben Tucker and Lenny McBrowne.
Concord's Desperado credits place Brown alongside Pat Martino, Eric Kloss, Eddie Green and Sherman Ferguson.

tyrone-brown.limitations: The Catalyst narrative describes his joining after the debut and does not establish an exact membership start date.
tyrone-brown.summary: Philadelphia bassist Tyrone Brown succeeded Alphonso Johnson in Catalyst and played in Pat Martino's Prestige-era bands for East! and Desperado.
tyrone-brown.why_it_matters: Craft's archival Catalyst reissue documents the personnel succession and confirms Brown's participation in separate Pat Martino recordings.

evidence.claim: Sireena Records' original Portrait product description identifies Trepte in the Irene Schweizer Trio (1966-1967) and Guru Guru (1968-1972).
Sireena's notes identify Trepte leading Spacebox (1975-1984) and Move Groove (1996-2001) and personally compiling Portrait.
The musician's preserved website links Trepte's performances with Guru Guru, Neu!, Faust, Spacebox and Move Groove and confirms his Portrait project.

uli-trepte.limitations: Portrait was published after Trepte's death although assembled by him, so its issue year is not a recording date for earlier bands.
uli-trepte.summary: German bassist Uli Trepte played in the Irene Schweizer Trio and Guru Guru, later led Spacebox and compiled his career album Portrait for Sireena.
uli-trepte.why_it_matters: The Sireena release catalog and Trepte's preserved artist site identify specific ensembles, recordings and his own retrospective selection.

evidence.claim: Snow appeared in the 1924 Sissle-Blake show also known as The Chocolate Dandies.
Snow headlined Chicago's Sunset Cafe in 1928 and had toured the Far East in 1926.

valaida-snow.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
valaida-snow.summary: Trumpeter-vocalist Valaida Snow appeared in the 1924 revue The Chocolate Dandies and led Chicago's Sunset Cafe bill in 1928 while touring widely as a performer.
valaida-snow.why_it_matters: Her trumpet playing challenges narrow accounts of women's early jazz roles.

evidence.claim: ECM credits Tsabropoulos on piano, Anja Lechner on cello and U.T. Gandhi on percussion for Melos (2008).
The ECM album credits Tsabropoulos as composer of Melos and Song of Gratitude.

vassilis-tsabropoulos.limitations: Artist-level historical synopsis; specific session credits restricted to cited primary material.
vassilis-tsabropoulos.summary: Greek pianist Vassilis Tsabropoulos combines piano improvisation with Byzantine-inspired composition in chamber recordings for ECM.
vassilis-tsabropoulos.why_it_matters: Documents concrete genre, performance and recording contributions to a diverse jazz catalog.

evidence.claim: The Louis Armstrong House Museum says she joined Armstrong's big band in 1942.
Its exhibition cites her appearances on Louis Armstrong Plays W.C. Handy and Satch Plays Fats.

velma-middleton.limitations: Birth year is disputed in museum archive; intentionally omitted.
velma-middleton.summary: Jazz singer Velma Middleton joined Louis Armstrong's band in 1942. She performed comic duets and sang on Armstrong albums Plays W.C. Handy and Satch Plays Fats.
velma-middleton.why_it_matters: Recovers a central female performer in Armstrong's touring ensemble.

evidence.claim: Nature Bliss dates Lampafeny to April 20, 2011 and its recording to January 2011 at Pannonia Studio in Budapest.
Its credits name Harcsa on vocals, Attila Blaho on piano and keys, Balint Gyemant on guitar and Gabor Subicz on trumpet for track nine.

veronika-harcsa.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
veronika-harcsa.summary: Hungarian singer Veronika Harcsa recorded Lampafeny in Budapest in January 2011 with pianist Attila Blaho and guitarist Balint Gyemant.
veronika-harcsa.why_it_matters: Jazz interpretation of Hungarian poetry joins small-ensemble vocals with modern harmonic textures.

evidence.claim: The Library of Congress National Jukebox catalogs Vic Berton as a songwriter, with Art Kassel, of Sobbin' Blues recorded August 17, 1923 by Benson Orchestra of Chicago for Victor 19130, matrix B-28432.
The Bix Beiderbecke record chronology identifies Vic Berton replacing Vic Moore on drums at the Wolverines' June 20, 1924 session, distinguishing it from May 6 takes.
The June 20, 1924 Gennett matrix inventory lists I Need Some Pettin', Royal Garden Blues and Tiger Rag in the Wolverines session associated with drummer Vic Berton.

vic-berton.limitations: The 1923 Sobbin' Blues recording identifies Berton only as songwriter, not performer. The June 1924 Wolverines sessions are documented through record-matrix research; individual take personnel can be disputed.
vic-berton.summary: Jazz drummer Vic Berton replaced Vic Moore for the Wolverines' June 1924 Gennett sessions and co-wrote Sobbin' Blues recorded by Victor in 1923.
vic-berton.why_it_matters: The Library of Congress' original Victor record shows an author credit, while a specialist chronological inventory of Gennett matrices establishes his actual drumming session.

evidence.claim: Genfan plays a percussive acoustic technique she calls slap-tap.
She appeared on the compilation La Guitara with female guitarists.
She won Guitar Player magazine's Guitar Superstar Competition.

vicki-genfan.limitations: Artist biography is promotional, and not every composition is jazz.
vicki-genfan.summary: Acoustic guitarist Vicki Genfan uses a slap-tap technique and appeared on the La Guitara compilation. She won Guitar Player magazine's Guitar Superstar competition.
vicki-genfan.why_it_matters: Her percussive solo approach connects folk, jazz and world-music guitar.

evidence.claim: Tower of Power's official discography names Victor Conte as the bassist on its original 1978 We Came to Play! album.
Sony Music's licensed 1978 recording credits identify Victor Conte playing bass and V. Conte among composers on Let Me Touch You from We Came to Play!.
The same 1978 original Sony catalog identifies Conte as bassist and co-composer of Love Bug, sung by drummer Ronnie Beck.
In a first-person career interview, Victor Conte recalls performing bass with Tower of Power in the 1970s and later working with Herbie Hancock in the early 1980s.

identity_resolution.method: Compared Tower of Power's own original 1978 line-up and Sony track-level rights credits with a first-person interview of bassist Victor Conte.
identity_resolution.note: The Tower of Power original lineup names Victor Conte on bass for We Came to Play, licensed Sony music credits separately identify the bassist and co-writer on two pieces, and Victor Conte's own interview recalls his 1970s Tower of Power bass work. They refer to the same person, distinct from other musicians with overlapping names; the evidence database has missing_p434 rather than a reciprocal MBID. No unverified MBID was arbitrarily selected.

victor-conte.limitations: This is the Victor Conte of Tower of Power, not an unrelated bassist: the band's named personnel and his own first-person interview connect the identities. The record is funk and R&B, not an original jazz band session.
victor-conte.summary: Bassist Victor Conte performed on Tower of Power's 1978 Columbia album We Came to Play! and co-wrote Let Me Touch You and Love Bug.
victor-conte.why_it_matters: The band's own discography and Sony's licensed original track credits identify two titles with Conte as both bassist and co-writer.

evidence.claim: Northwestern identifies Goines as clarinetist and saxophonist.
It says he joined the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra and Marsalis Septet in 1993.

victor-goines.limitations: Historical 2016 faculty notice; do not present title as current.
victor-goines.summary: New Orleans clarinetist and saxophonist Victor Goines performed with the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra and Wynton Marsalis Septet. He also led jazz studies at Northwestern.
victor-goines.why_it_matters: Connects contemporary orchestral jazz performance and education.

evidence.claim: Victor Noriega's own project page identifies his jazz piano-trio album Alay (2006) as an exploration of Filipino folk themes.
The composer's own site says the Oakland East Bay Symphony commissioned Generations, Directions in 2012 as a seven-movement orchestral work.
Jack Straw Cultural Center's artist-program archive identifies Noriega's recordings Stone's Throw (2004), Alay (2006), and Fenceless (2008).

victor-noriega.limitations: The 2012 orchestral commission is a separate project from his jazz-trio albums; no award year is assigned without direct records.
victor-noriega.summary: Filipino American jazz pianist Victor Noriega released Stone's Throw and Alay, and composed Generations, Directions for Oakland East Bay Symphony.
victor-noriega.why_it_matters: The composer's own project documentation and an institutional artist-residency archive identify tangible albums and a commissioned suite.

evidence.claim: Delmark original Sound of Joy album notes credit Victor Sproles on bass in Sun Ra Arkestra sessions recorded in 1957.
Concord original Battle Stations notes identify Victor Sproles in Eddie Lockjaw Davis and Johnny Griffin rhythm section alongside Norman Simmons and Ben Riley.
Concord The Red Rodney Quintets notes place Victor Sproles among the original sessions with Red Rodney and Ira Sullivan.

victor-sproles.limitations: The Sun Ra album was originally intended for Transition and then issued by Delmark; reissue publication date is distinct from the 1957 sessions.
victor-sproles.summary: Chicago jazz bassist Victor Sproles recorded with Sun Ra on Sound of Joy and backed Eddie Davis and Johnny Griffin on Battle Stations.
victor-sproles.why_it_matters: Delmark original recording personnel and Concord original album notes establish independent sessions for a documented Chicago bassist.

evidence.claim: The Radio Swiss Jazz catalog credits Victoria Abril on vocals for Mais que nada with Rosa Passos providing guitar and additional vocals.
Radio Swiss Jazz separately credits Abril as vocalist for Desde que samba e samba, from Putcheros do Brasil, recorded in Madrid in October 2004.

victoria-abril.limitations: These are crossover Brazilian repertoire performances recorded in Madrid in 2004; do not infer earlier jazz instrumental experience.
victoria-abril.summary: Victoria Abril sang the bossa nova titles Mais que nada and Desde que samba e samba for the 2005 Putcheros do Brasil album.
victoria-abril.why_it_matters: Radio Swiss Jazz's track-level catalog individually identifies the vocalist and recording program.

evidence.claim: ECM lists Vincent Chancey on French horn in Brass Fantasy alongside Lester Bowie, four trumpeters, two trombonists, tuba and drums.
Avant Pop was recorded March 1986 at Tonstudio Bauer, Ludwigsburg, and released September 29, 1986.

vincent-chancey.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
vincent-chancey.summary: French horn player Vincent Chancey joined Lester Bowie's nine-piece Brass Fantasy for Avant Pop, recorded at Tonstudio Bauer in March 1986.
vincent-chancey.why_it_matters: His French horn widens the brass ensemble's register and contrapuntal color.

evidence.claim: Original dml-records artist shop credits Vincent Klink on bass trumpet with Patrick Bebelaar on piano, Michel Godard, Gavino Murgia and Carlo Rizzo for Stupor Mundi, catalog CD 034, year 2014.
Patrick Bebelaar's own discography lists the 2014 Stupor Mundi instrumental lineup, including Vincent Klink playing bass trumpet.
Bayerischer Rundfunk's July 29, 2016 broadcast page identifies Klink as a bass-trumpet player whose jazz performances it recorded for a radio feature.
The German Record Critics Award's original 2015/1 list awards Stupor Mundi with named performers Klink, Bebelaar, Godard, Murgia and Rizzo on DML Records 033.

vincent-klink.limitations: Stupor Mundi was recorded and copyrighted in 2014, while several download retailers give later digital release dates; the 2015 award pertains to the project, not a separate performance.
vincent-klink.summary: German bass-trumpeter Vincent Klink joined Patrick Bebelaar's Stupor Mundi project, recorded in 2014, and appeared on Bavarian Radio jazz programming in 2016.
vincent-klink.why_it_matters: The original dml-records project, Bebelaar's musician discography and Bavarian public radio independently establish Klink as an actual performing musician.

evidence.claim: Fresh Sound's reissue session details credit Vinnie Burke with Eddie Costa, Jimmy Raney and Joe Morello on a New York July 22, 1956 ABC-Paramount All-Stars date.
The same reissue identifies Burke on bass, Dick Wetmore on violin, Calo Scott on cello and Bobby Grillo on guitar in String Jazz Quartet, recorded January 10, 1957.
Fresh Sound's individual Jubilee Records JLP 1025 catalog identifies Eddie Costa, Vinnie Burke and Nick Stabulas on the 1956 Eddie Costa-Vinnie Burke Trio record.

vinnie-burke.limitations: Original sessions are 1956 and 1957; the Fresh Sound CD compilation date must not be mistaken for recording dates. The short label biography reproduces AllMusic and is not used as evidence.
vinnie-burke.summary: Double bassist Vinnie Burke recorded 1956 ABC-Paramount All-Stars sessions and a 1957 String Jazz Quartet album with Dick Wetmore and Calo Scott.
vinnie-burke.why_it_matters: The reissuing label reconstructs original ABC-Paramount sessions by matrix groups and identifies a later distinct quartet instrumentation.

evidence.claim: The Recording Academy credits Colaiuta on the Grammy-winning Five Peace Band - Live album.
It includes him among credited performers on the Grammy-nominated The Wind Cries Mary recording.

vinnie-colaiuta.limitations: Recording Academy nominations alone do not establish the instrument played on each track.
vinnie-colaiuta.summary: Drummer Vinnie Colaiuta performed on John McLaughlin's Five Peace Band Live and contributed to The Wind Cries Mary with Sting and McLaughlin, according to Grammy credits.
vinnie-colaiuta.why_it_matters: Verifiable jazz-to-pop crossover through recording credits.

evidence.claim: Fresh Sound's Nocturne restoration lists Gonsalves on baritone sax with Bob Enevoldsen, Buddy Wise, Lou Levy, Harry Babasin and Larry Bunker, recorded September 29, 1954.
The Liberty LJH-6010 Jazz San Francisco Style original November 1955 sessions credit Gonsalves on baritone with Dan Patiris and Clyde Pound.
The same archival original-label reconstruction credits him on the Rudy Salvini Big Band's November 1956 Sands Ballroom session in Oakland.

virgil-gonsalves.limitations: The modern compilations are later releases; original sessions were in 1954 and 1955. Both label reconstructions are published by Fresh Sound.
virgil-gonsalves.summary: Baritone saxophonist Virgil Gonsalves recorded a 1954 Nocturne sextet with Lou Levy and a 1955 Liberty sextet with Dan Patiris and Clyde Pound.
virgil-gonsalves.why_it_matters: Separate Nocturne and Liberty album restorations identify exact recorded sessions and participating musicians.

evidence.claim: RAI Teche original television archive identifies Virgilio Savona as a Quartetto Cetra performer in Biblioteca Studio Uno filmed in 1964.
RAI's 1964-1966 variety-program catalog credits Tata Giacobetti and Virgilio Savona as authors of Cetra 66 broadcast February 24, 1966.
RAI Teche artist index connects Savona to its preserved 1964 Biblioteca Studio Uno segment.

virgilio-savona.limitations: The accessible program details are television archival facts, not proof of specific album release dates or of every song's jazz classification.
virgilio-savona.summary: Italian singer and pianist Virgilio Savona performed with Quartetto Cetra in a 1964 RAI broadcast and co-wrote the 1966 television program Cetra 66.
virgilio-savona.why_it_matters: RAI's own television archive identifies an individual performance and a distinct writing credit within Quartetto Cetra.

evidence.claim: ECM names Volker Kriegel on guitar among the featured musicians of the Jazz Ensemble des HR anthology Atmospheric Conditions Permitting.
The anthology comprises recordings made at Hessischer Rundfunk in Frankfurt from 1967 to 1993 and was first released October 1, 1995.

volker-kriegel.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
volker-kriegel.summary: German guitarist Volker Kriegel features on ECM's Atmospheric Conditions Permitting, a Hessischer Rundfunk jazz-ensemble collection spanning 1967 to 1993.
volker-kriegel.why_it_matters: His presence reflects the German radio jazz scene where modern composition met fusion.

evidence.claim: Milt Jackson heard Legge playing bass in Buffalo and recommended him to Dizzy Gillespie.
Legge remained in Gillespie's group through 1954 and later played on Sonny Rollins's Plays for Bird.

wade-legge.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
wade-legge.summary: Pianist Wade Legge joined Dizzy Gillespie after being heard as a bassist by Milt Jackson; he later recorded with Sonny Rollins and Charles Mingus.
wade-legge.why_it_matters: A short-lived but flexible modern-jazz sideman heard on key 1950s small-group recordings.

evidence.claim: The official Miles Davis collaborator page identifies Wallace Roney as a trumpet player who performed with Miles at Montreux in 1991.
The Miles Davis estate states that Wallace Roney played with Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers and in drummer Tony Williams' band.
The official Miles Davis concert film page names Wallace Roney among the featured soloists in the July 1991 Quincy Jones Montreux concert.

wallace-roney.limitations: The Miles Davis estate identifies the Montreux collaboration but does not justify treating all of Roney's own albums as Miles Davis recordings.
wallace-roney.summary: Trumpeter Wallace Roney played with Art Blakey and Tony Williams and appeared alongside Miles Davis at Montreux in 1991 for music arranged by Gil Evans.
wallace-roney.why_it_matters: The Miles Davis estate catalog gives a specific 1991 concert and associates the trumpeter with two major jazz ensembles.

evidence.claim: Walt Weiskopf official biography dates his New York Buddy Rich Big Band debut to 1981 at age 21.
The same biography specifies Simplicity as a Criss Cross Jazz leader album from 1993 and describes his own original composition practice.

walt-weiskopf.limitations: A 1981 band affiliation does not establish his appearance on all Buddy Rich records; Simplicity year is album rather than session date.
walt-weiskopf.summary: Saxophonist Walt Weiskopf played in Buddy Rich Big Band in 1981 and issued the leader album Simplicity for Criss Cross in 1993.
walt-weiskopf.why_it_matters: His official musician biography describes the early big-band career and a first named leader-era album with a label/year.

evidence.claim: Chicago Public Library documents Walter Henri Dyett as music and band instructor at DuSable High School from 1935 to 1966.
The library names Nat King Cole, Dorothy Donegan, Dinah Washington, Johnny Griffin and Gene Ammons among Dyett's music students.
The University of Chicago's Maps of the Stacks project documents Dyett's Hi-Jinks revue and his papers' 500 performance and family photographs.

identity_resolution.note: The archival named Walter Henri Dyett and exact DuSable bandmaster work identify the seed person without relying on an unconfirmed MusicBrainz crosslink.

walter-dyett.limitations: No reciprocal MusicBrainz link is accepted as identity proof. His complete name Walter Henri Dyett, 1901 birth and DuSable career are separately matched to original institutional archives.
walter-dyett.summary: Chicago bandmaster Walter Dyett taught Nat King Cole, Johnny Griffin and Dinah Washington while directing the music program at DuSable High School.
walter-dyett.why_it_matters: An original Chicago Public Library finding aid identifies his full name, personal archival papers, teaching positions and named students.

evidence.claim: The Recording Academy lists A Fifth of Beethoven as a 1977 Pop Instrumental nominee.
It also lists a nomination connected with Family Guy Live in Vegas in 2006.

walter-murphy.limitations: Disco and pop/comedy credit; evidence does not establish a core jazz identity.
walter-murphy.summary: Composer and arranger Walter Murphy adapted classical themes for disco, earning a Grammy nomination for A Fifth of Beethoven, and worked on Family Guy Live in Vegas.
walter-murphy.why_it_matters: Marks the boundary of instrumental crossover in a jazz-related catalogue.

evidence.claim: Blue Note announced return to casual as Walter Smith III Blue Note debut released April 7 2023, following still casual from 2014.
The label credits pianist Taylor Eigsti, guitarist Matt Stevens, bassist Harish Raghavan and drummer Kendrick Scott on return to casual; trumpeter Ambrose Akinmusire guests.

walter-smith-iii.limitations: The Blue Note physical LP shop metadata lists a later 2023 release date for one format; label original debut announcement says April 7.
walter-smith-iii.summary: Tenor saxophonist Walter Smith III released Blue Note debut return to casual in 2023 with Taylor Eigsti, Matt Stevens and Kendrick Scott.
walter-smith-iii.why_it_matters: The label documents original collaborators on a modern straight-ahead jazz record and separates studio/single lineups.

evidence.claim: ECM credits Warren Smith on marimba and percussion with Jeanne Lee on voice, John Abercrombie on guitar and Enrico Rava on trumpet.
Quotation Marks combines sessions from December 1973 and April 1974 and has an original release date of June 1, 1976.

warren-smith.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
warren-smith.summary: Percussionist Warren Smith recorded on Enrico Rava's Quotation Marks, an adventurous album with Jeanne Lee, John Abercrombie and Jack DeJohnette.
warren-smith.why_it_matters: His marimba and percussion brought additional textures to Rava's exploratory ensemble.

evidence.claim: Mack Avenue says Tisdale released his first solo album in 1995 while still playing in the NBA.
The label lists Rebound, Way Up and Hang Time among its Wayman Tisdale albums.

wayman-tisdale.limitations: Only claims recorded in the cited artist, label, institution or original archive are included; crossovers are not classified exclusively as jazz.
wayman-tisdale.summary: American electric bassist Wayman Tisdale pursued smooth jazz recording alongside professional basketball, releasing several leader albums.
wayman-tisdale.why_it_matters: Documents specific recordings, ensembles or performance roles and their place in jazz or adjacent genres.

evidence.claim: Concord's Side Effect reissue identifies Wayne Henderson as trombonist, producer and writer of Keep That Same Old Feeling, earlier recorded with the Crusaders.
That reissue says Henderson soloed under the pseudonym Big Daddy on Side Effect's Keep That Same Old Feeling.
Concord credits Henderson as producer of Pleasure's Dust Yourself Off (1975) and Accept No Substitutes (1976).

wayne-henderson.limitations: The Side Effect solo credited to his pseudonym Big Daddy is specific to that recording; the article does not list his entire Crusaders discography.
wayne-henderson.summary: Jazz Crusaders trombonist Wayne Henderson wrote Keep That Same Old Feeling and produced 1970s soul-funk projects for Side Effect and Pleasure.
wayne-henderson.why_it_matters: Original Fantasy reissue notes distinguish Henderson's instrumental, songwriting and production activities.

evidence.claim: Krantz's own discography lists 2 Drink Minimum (1995) with Zach Danziger and Lincoln Goines.
His official site lists Krantz Carlock Lefebvre (2009) with Keith Carlock and Tim Lefebvre.

wayne-krantz.limitations: Artist-level historical synopsis; specific session credits restricted to cited primary material.
wayne-krantz.summary: American guitarist Wayne Krantz leads electric improvising groups and recorded with drummers Zach Danziger and Keith Carlock.
wayne-krantz.why_it_matters: Documents concrete genre, performance and recording contributions to a diverse jazz catalog.

evidence.claim: Leipzig music university says Neumann has held its jazz guitar professorship since 2006.
Its biography names collaborations with Richie Beirach and Napoleon Murphy Brock.

werner-neumann.summary: German jazz guitarist Werner Neumann teaches at Leipzig and has performed with Richie Beirach and Napoleon Murphy Brock.
werner-neumann.why_it_matters: Documents this musician's distinctive role in jazz and related music.

evidence.claim: Clean Feed's Fierce Silence lists Whit Dickey on drums and Kirk Knuffke on cornet, with compositions jointly credited to both.
The album was recorded October 14, 2015 by Jim Clouse at Park West Studio, Brooklyn, and produced by Whit Dickey.

whit-dickey.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
whit-dickey.summary: Drummer Whit Dickey recorded the cornet-drums duo Fierce Silence with Kirk Knuffke in Brooklyn on October 14, 2015.
whit-dickey.why_it_matters: Their spacious free-jazz ballads explore restraint and silence as improvisational devices.

evidence.claim: Ware worked with Monk and Coltrane in 1957
Also played in Rollins Village Vanguard concerts in 1957

wilbur-ware.limitations: Source-specific musical details; does not establish exhaustive discography.
wilbur-ware.summary: Bassist Wilbur Ware anchored Thelonious Monk's 1957 groups with John Coltrane and played Sonny Rollins's 'A Night at the Village Vanguard' sessions.
wilbur-ware.why_it_matters: Syncopated, spacious low-register bass foundation in major hard-bop sessions

evidence.claim: Frank Newton trumpet with Billie Holiday in New York April 20 1939
In April 1939, Frankie Newton played trumpet on Billie Holiday's recordings of 'Strange Fruit' and 'Fine and Mellow'.

william-frank-newton.limitations: Specific sourced music facts, not a comprehensive discography.
william-frank-newton.summary: Trumpeter Frankie Newton backed Billie Holiday's April 1939 Commodore recordings of 'Strange Fruit' and 'Fine and Mellow' in his Cafe Society Orchestra.
william-frank-newton.why_it_matters: Early jazz trumpeter on culturally pivotal Billie Holiday session

evidence.claim: The Recording Academy lists ten Grammy nominations credited to Felder.
Its records include Felder's Inherit the Wind and Crusaders albums Rural Renewal and Images.

wilton-felder.limitations: The Recording Academy profile confirms credited projects, not his exact instrument or compositions.
wilton-felder.summary: Wilton Felder appeared on acclaimed recordings with the Crusaders and earned Grammy nominations under his name. These projects moved between R&B and instrumental jazz.
wilton-felder.why_it_matters: Tracks the Crusaders' crossover into R&B and contemporary jazz.

evidence.claim: Manone published an autobiography titled Trumpet on the Wing.
He made Las Vegas his permanent home in 1954.
The UNLV archive holds Manone papers donated by Joseph Manone Jr.

wingy-manone.limitations: Institutional finding aid summarizes estate collection, not individual record session personnel.
wingy-manone.summary: Trumpeter Wingy Manone wrote and arranged scores and published the autobiography Trumpet on the Wing. He settled in Las Vegas in 1954 and played in hotels while touring.
wingy-manone.why_it_matters: A donated family archive grounds his jazz career in original papers and performance history.

evidence.claim: We Are Busy Bodies' licensed reissue was released November 27, 2020, remastered by Noah Mintz from original quarter-inch tapes.
The album's 1968 quartet featured saxophonist Ngozi, pianist Lionel Pillay, bassist Agrippa Magwaza, and drummer Early Mabuza.

winston-mankunku-ngozi.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
winston-mankunku-ngozi.summary: South African tenor saxophonist Winston Mankunku Ngozi recorded Yakhal' Inkomo in 1968 with Lionel Pillay, Agrippa Magwaza and Early Mabuza.
winston-mankunku-ngozi.why_it_matters: An apartheid-era South African tenor jazz landmark with a distinct original lament.

evidence.claim: ECM's 2016 'Rising Grace' featured Wolfgang Muthspiel, Ambrose Akinmusire, Brad Mehldau, Larry Grenadier and Brian Blade.
Album personnel included Akinmusire, Mehldau, Grenadier and Blade.

wolfgang-muthspiel.limitations: Research is source-specific; credits denote actual documented roles, not an exhaustive discography.
wolfgang-muthspiel.summary: Guitarist Wolfgang Muthspiel led ECM's 'Rising Grace' (2016) with Ambrose Akinmusire, Brad Mehldau, Larry Grenadier and Brian Blade.
wolfgang-muthspiel.why_it_matters: Guitar-led chamber jazz with equal improvisational ensemble roles.

evidence.claim: ECM dates Then Comes the White Tiger to October 1, 1994 and its recording to May 1993 at Garak Studio, Seoul.
ECM credits Puschnig on alto saxophone and alto flute, Kim Duk Soo on changgo and piri, and Linda Sharrock on vocals.

wolfgang-puschnig.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
wolfgang-puschnig.summary: Austrian reed player Wolfgang Puschnig recorded with Red Sun and Korean percussion group SamulNori in Seoul in May 1993 for ECM's White Tiger.
wolfgang-puschnig.why_it_matters: Shows transcontinental jazz improvisation with Korean rhythmic instruments and jazz saxophone.

evidence.claim: Intakt credits Wolter Wierbos on trombone alongside Christof Thewes and Gerhard Gschlossl in Globe Unity Orchestra.
The Globe Unity - 50 Years concert was recorded at Jazzfest Berlin on November 4, 2016 and issued as Intakt Recording 298 in 2018.

wolter-wierbos.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
wolter-wierbos.summary: Trombonist Wolter Wierbos played at Jazzfest Berlin in 2016 with Alexander von Schlippenbach's Globe Unity Orchestra for its fiftieth anniversary.
wolter-wierbos.why_it_matters: His playing contributes to a large-scale European free-jazz brass and reed ensemble.

evidence.claim: Dutch public broadcaster NPO Radio 2 says Wouter Hamel made his North Sea Jazz Festival debut in 2005 and released Hamel in 2007.
NPO Radio 2 identifies Nobody's Tune as his second album and describes his third, Lohengrin, as self-produced.
ESNS's artist profile identifies Benny Sings as a collaborator and describes Hamel's album Pompadour as a stylistic shift from Lohengrin.
Wouter Hamel's own Bandcamp discography lists Hamel, Nobody's Tune, Lohengrin and Pompadour as releases under his artist account.

wouter-hamel.limitations: Originally evidence_candidate; the artist's music crosses jazz and pop. NPO's album chronology and ESNS's six-album-era biography reflect their respective publication periods, not current total discography.
wouter-hamel.summary: Dutch jazz-pop singer Wouter Hamel made his North Sea Jazz Festival debut in 2005 and released Hamel, Nobody's Tune and the self-produced Lohengrin.
wouter-hamel.why_it_matters: Dutch public broadcaster NPO, an international festival biography and the artist's own album catalog document his trajectory beyond generic genre labeling.

evidence.claim: Fresh Sound's RCA Victor Basses Loaded reissue identifies Wyatt Bull Ruther as solo bass leader on tracks 9-12 recorded January 29, 1955 in New York.
Fresh Sound's Boots Mussulli / Toshiko Akiyoshi Storyville restoration credits Ruther on bass with Akiyoshi and Ed Thigpen at a July 1956 session.
Fresh Sound's Playtime reissue lists Ruther on bass in unreleased Buddy Rich Argo sessions circa January 1961 and in October 1961 NBC broadcasts.

wyatt-ruther.limitations: All three accounts are archival reissue research from one record company; recording dates in 1955, 1956 and 1961 are distinct from modern CD reissues.
wyatt-ruther.summary: Bassist Wyatt Ruther led a 1955 Basses Loaded date and joined Toshiko Akiyoshi's quartet in 1956 and Buddy Rich's small group in 1961.
wyatt-ruther.why_it_matters: Fresh Sound's three independently described original-label sessions identify specific ensembles and recording locations.

evidence.claim: Rock Hall's archival catalogue lists original King recordings in a Wynonie Harris compilation.
Its track list includes Good Rockin' Tonight and Good Morning Judge with Harris credited on vocals.

wynonie-harris.limitations: Rock Hall discography confirms tracks and vocalist but not individual recording personnel.
wynonie-harris.summary: Blues shouter Wynonie Harris recorded Good Rockin' Tonight and Good Morning Judge for King Records. His rhythm-and-blues recordings helped shape early rock-and-roll singing.
wynonie-harris.why_it_matters: Connects jump blues vocals and the early rock-and-roll repertory.

evidence.claim: Kelly recorded fourteen trio titles for Blue Note in 1951.
He worked with Miles Davis from 1959 to 1963 then formed a trio with Paul Chambers and Jimmy Cobb.

wynton-kelly.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
wynton-kelly.summary: Pianist Wynton Kelly recorded fourteen Blue Note trio tracks in 1951, played with Miles Davis from 1959 to 1963 and then formed a trio with Paul Chambers and Jimmy Cobb.
wynton-kelly.why_it_matters: His lyrical swing drove post-bop rhythm sections.

evidence.claim: Universal Music lists Blue Note Everyday released August 28 2015.
Album credits include Yaron Herman on piano and Ziv Ravitz on drums and percussion.

yaron-herman.limitations: Research is source-specific; credits denote actual documented roles, not an exhaustive discography.
yaron-herman.summary: Jazz pianist Yaron Herman released the Blue Note album 'Everyday' (2015) with drummer Ziv Ravitz, linking solo piano and percussive textures.
yaron-herman.why_it_matters: Modern jazz piano with small-group rhythmic experimentation.

evidence.claim: The University of Canterbury audio library catalog identifies Yehudi Menuhin and Stephane Grappelli as violinists on a 1988 EMI compilation of 1972 to 1983 recordings.
Warner Classics recording credits identify Jealousy recorded at Abbey Road March 7 1973 with Menuhin and Grappelli, with arrangements by Max Harris.

yehudi-menuhin.limitations: The 1988 CD is a compilation of 1972, 1973, 1977, 1979 and 1983 recordings; avoid calling every track a 1973 session.
yehudi-menuhin.summary: Classical violinist Yehudi Menuhin recorded swing standards with jazz violinist Stephane Grappelli, including Jealousy at Abbey Road in 1973.
yehudi-menuhin.why_it_matters: University catalog and original Warner Classics label data identify two individual violinists on dated collaboration sessions.

evidence.claim: University of the Pacific's Holt-Atherton Special Collections preserves a 2012 interview with Yolande Bavan identifying her as vocalist in The Real Ambassadors at the 1962 Monterey Jazz Festival.
The University of the Pacific history describes The Real Ambassadors as a Dave and Iola Brubeck jazz musical recorded in 1961 and performed live once.
A contemporary July 1962 DownBeat interview reported Yolande Bavan joining Dave Lambert and Jon Hendricks after Annie Ross left the vocal group.

yolande-bavan.limitations: Original archival descriptions document the Monterey performance; later retrospective dates of every Lambert, Hendricks and Bavan engagement are not inferred.
yolande-bavan.summary: Ceylon-born jazz singer Yolande Bavan succeeded Annie Ross in the Lambert and Hendricks vocal trio and sang in The Real Ambassadors at Monterey in 1962.
yolande-bavan.why_it_matters: The University of the Pacific holds first-person interviews documenting the 1962 Brubeck stage production, while period reporting confirms her group transition.

evidence.claim: Melon catalogs Younha's debut single Yubikiri in September 2004.
Her studio album End Theory was released in 2021.
Her seventh album Growth Theory appeared September 2024.

younha.limitations: Original Korean commercial catalog confirms releases; career is pop rather than jazz, so reviewer may exclude.
younha.summary: Korean pianist and singer-songwriter Younha debuted in Japan in 2004. Her 2021 album End Theory includes Oort Cloud; Growth Theory followed in 2024.
younha.why_it_matters: Her pop and rock catalog adds stylistic range beyond mainstream jazz.

evidence.claim: Drummer Klaus Kugel's original discography credits Yuri Yaremchuk with soprano and tenor saxophones, clarinet and bass clarinet on YATOKU with Mark Tokar and Kugel, recorded in Krakow in 2006 and released by NotTwo in 2007.
Zeromoon Records' original Live at Improvdom credits Yuri Yaremchuk on soprano saxophone and bass clarinet alongside Alexei Borisov's live electronics and voice.
The Zeromoon label dates the duo's concert at Moscow's Club Club to December 23, 2025 and the album's issue to January 11, 2026.

identity_resolution.method: Crossmatched the original Klaus Kugel musician discography with the named performer and instrumentation in the Zeromoon label's later original concert recording.
identity_resolution.note: Both original recording sources identify improvising saxophonist and bass-clarinetist Yuri Yaremchuk: on YATOKU with Mark Tokar and Klaus Kugel in 2006, and later on an original live electronic-improvisation duo release with Alexei Borisov. The queue records missing_p434, not reciprocal MusicBrainz identity; no MBID was guessed or selected, and no identifier was used as historical biographical proof.

yuri-yaremchuk.limitations: The 2006 YATOKU date denotes recording in Krakow and 2007 the NotTwo release; the Borisov concert was December 2025 and Zeromoon released the recording in January 2026.
yuri-yaremchuk.summary: Ukrainian saxophonist Yuri Yaremchuk recorded YATOKU with Mark Tokar and Klaus Kugel in 2006 and a 2025 duo performance with Alexei Borisov.
yuri-yaremchuk.why_it_matters: Two performers' original recordings independently identify Yaremchuk, his woodwinds, collaborating musicians and specific sessions separated by nineteen years.

evidence.claim: Oberlin Conservatory reports jazz violinist Zach Brock joined its faculty for fall 2026 as associate professor of multi-genre performance and improvisation.
The same conservatory credits Brock as a longstanding Snarky Puppy member playing on 2016 Culcha Vulcha, 2022 Empire Central and 2025 Somni.

zach-brock.limitations: Oberlin lists these as band albums on which Brock recorded; Grammy wins are collective, not solo awards; appointment is not a recorded session.
zach-brock.summary: Jazz violinist Zach Brock played in Snarky Puppy on Culcha Vulcha (2016) and Empire Central (2022), then joined Oberlin faculty in 2026.
zach-brock.why_it_matters: Oberlin conservatory professional biography provides recording credits and jazz-improvisation faculty appointment.

evidence.claim: Mike Mainieri's original NYC Records catalog lists Zachary Breaux on guitar and vocals for Laidback and credits Toots Thielemans on harmonica.
Japan's NII scholarly library catalog identifies the 1994 Laidback CD and its recording at River Sound Studios, New York.
Texas State Historical Association identifies Breaux as a guitarist with Roy Ayers Ubiquity and documents his leader releases Groovin', Laidback and Uptown Groove.

zachary-breaux.limitations: Conflicting reports of his death date are not repeated; 1994 refers to the original album.
zachary-breaux.summary: Guitarist Zachary Breaux performed with Roy Ayers and released his NYC Records album Laidback in 1994, featuring harmonica guest Toots Thielemans.
zachary-breaux.why_it_matters: The musician's original record label, university record catalog and Texas historical archive establish specific work.

evidence.claim: His official discography dates Shakti to 1975 and Song for Everyone on ECM to 1985.
The Recording Academy credits As We Speak to Hussain, Bela Fleck, Edgar Meyer and Rakesh Chaurasia.

zakir-hussain.limitations: Indian classical musician and global collaborator, not exclusively jazz.
zakir-hussain.summary: Indian tabla player Zakir Hussain recorded with Shakti and worked across Indian classical, world music and jazz, including ECM albums and the 2023 As We Speak.
zakir-hussain.why_it_matters: Highlights tabla's dialogue with jazz and other improvisational traditions.

evidence.claim: MPS names Zbigniew Seifert, Joachim Kuhn, Cecil McBee, Billy Hart and Jasper van't Hof in the personnel of Man of the Light.
The MPS label dates Man of the Light to 1977 and describes Stillness as a violin-and-bass duet and Love in the Garden as a duo with keyboardist Jasper van't Hof.

zbigniew-seifert.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
zbigniew-seifert.summary: Polish violinist Zbigniew Seifert recorded Man of the Light with Joachim Kuhn, Cecil McBee and Billy Hart in 1976; MPS released the album in 1977.
zbigniew-seifert.why_it_matters: Seifert brought saxophone-like post-Coltrane phrasing to violin-led modern jazz.

evidence.claim: Phantom Orchard duo is Parkins and Mori
2004 album Phantom Orchard documented in artist discography

zeena-parkins.limitations: Source-specific musical details, not a complete discography.
zeena-parkins.summary: Electric-harp improviser Zeena Parkins formed Phantom Orchard with electronic musician Ikue Mori, recording their self-titled 2004 album.
zeena-parkins.why_it_matters: Electric-harp techniques and electronics in downtown New York free improvisation

evidence.claim: The International Trumpet Guild identifies Ziggy Elman as Harry Aaron Finkelman and records his entry into Benny Goodman's trumpet section in 1936.
The guild's historical note states that Elman joined Tommy Dorsey's band in 1940 after Goodman paused band activities.
The same guild account describes Elman's band recording And the Angels Sing and identifies it as a 1939 hit.

ziggy-elman.limitations: The guild narrative does not give a matrix or session number for And the Angels Sing, and its chart description is not cross-checked against contemporary Billboard issues.
ziggy-elman.summary: Trumpeter Ziggy Elman played with Benny Goodman and Tommy Dorsey, and his own band recorded And the Angels Sing, a hit in 1939.
ziggy-elman.why_it_matters: The International Trumpet Guild preserves the musician's name history, band affiliations and the later provenance of his King trumpet.

evidence.claim: Ngqawana's official site names Zimology, Ingoma, Zimphonic Suites and Vadzimu as his four studio albums issued on Sheer Sound.
His official biography lists soprano, alto, tenor and baritone saxophones, concert flute, piccolo, piano and vocals among his instruments.

zim-ngqawana.limitations: Specific source-reviewed music claims; not a comprehensive discography.
zim-ngqawana.summary: South African reed player Zim Ngqawana released four Sheer Sound studio albums: Zimology, Ingoma, Zimphonic Suites and Vadzimu.
zim-ngqawana.why_it_matters: Free-minded South African improvisation ties multi-instrumental playing to spirituality.

evidence.claim: Jive Music says Weinrich began violin at age eight and played early concerts at Vienna's Jazzland.
The label names collaborative playing with Barney Kessel, Attila Zoller and Art Farmer.

zipflo-weinrich.limitations: Only claims recorded in the cited artist, label, institution or original archive are included; crossovers are not classified exclusively as jazz.
zipflo-weinrich.summary: Austrian jazz violinist Zipflo Weinrich drew on Sinti swing traditions and recorded with international jazz musicians while developing his own sound.
zipflo-weinrich.why_it_matters: Documents specific recordings, ensembles or performance roles and their place in jazz or adjacent genres.

evidence.claim: Whittington Music Festival describes her album Colour of Sound.
Its biography identifies projects with her brother Idris Rahman and study at Berklee.

zoe-rahman.limitations: Festival biography is original presenter material but borrows promotional text.
zoe-rahman.summary: British jazz pianist Zoe Rahman combines classical study with Bengali musical roots. Her work includes Colour of Sound and collaborations with her brother Idris Rahman.
zoe-rahman.why_it_matters: Documents contemporary British jazz reflecting multiple cultural traditions.

evidence.claim: Drummer Zutty Singleton played in Louis Armstrong's 1928 Hot Five sessions with pianist Earl Hines.
The July 1928 Hot Five sessions included Earl Hines, Louis Armstrong and Zutty Singleton.

zutty-singleton.limitations: Research is source-specific; credits denote actual documented roles, not an exhaustive discography.
zutty-singleton.summary: New Orleans drummer Zutty Singleton played on Louis Armstrong's 1928 Hot Five 'Knee Drops' and 'West End Blues' era sessions with Earl Hines.
zutty-singleton.why_it_matters: Early New Orleans rhythmic style in important Armstrong small groups.
